rows.why: Item 7 asks what happens when a newly drawn code repeats an existing one. S1 says it is drawn again, and the pick redraws (up to 100 tries before throwing). No item asks about the 14-day expiry or the 'unused' starting state as such, though item 6's run shows both.
No item asks whether redeeming grants access to that task and no other. Item 11 covers usedBy/usedAt, but it is about list output and fits S9 better.
Item 5 asks how case, whitespace and hyphens are handled. The pick normalises all three, and the run redeemed a lowercase code with spaces and hyphens successfully.

Item 1 asks whether a code is still valid at exactly 14 days. The pick treats now >= createdAt + 14 days as expired, and the run at exactly 14 days returned reason 'expired'. That fits S4, where redeeming works 1 ms before and fails at the exact moment.

No item asks what happens when the same contributor redeems their own used code again, which is what S5 settles (it succeeds and nothing changes). Item 2 is about which reason wins when a code is both used and expired or revoked. Item 3 is about a different, unused code for a task the contributor can already access.

Item 4 asks what redeeming a code that doesn't exist does. The run returned { ok: false, reason: 'unknown' }, as S6 expects. Item 8 covers the 'used code cannot be revoked' clause, but S6 is mainly about redemption being refused.
Item 3 asks exactly this question. The run shows a second code failing with 'already has access' and that code staying 'unused'.
Item 10 asks how overlapping calls are handled. The run used a store with delayed calls and concurrent redeems: exactly one succeeded and the others failed with 'used'.

Item 11 asks what list returns. The pick and the run show code, createdAt, expiresAt and state (unused/used/revoked/expired), with usedBy/usedAt on used codes. Item 2's run also shows a used code still listed as 'used' after its expiry time.
